Vietnam Evacuates 350,000 as Typhoon Kalmaegi Nears..

Authorities in #Vietnam’s Gia Lai Province are evacuating about 350,000 residents as Typhoon #Kalmaegi regains strength over the South China Sea. The Vietnamese government has mobilized emergency forces and pre-positioned shelters and resources in preparation for the storm’s landfall.
Meanwhile, in the #Philippines, Typhoon Kalmaegi locally name #Tino has left at least 140 people dead and 127 missing following devastating floods and flash-flooding across central regions, particularly in #Cebu Province. Relief operations continue despite widespread infrastructure damage and blocked roads.

This comes after leaving a trail of devastation and over 100 dead in the Philippines.

-Current Winds: ~140 km/h (87 mph), potentially intensifying to over 160 km/h before landfall.

-Path: Moving West-Northwest towards central Vietnamese provinces Quang Ngai, Dak Lak.

-Extreme winds, 4-8 meter waves, storm surge and severe flooding/landslides likely.

10AM NEWS WRAP UP - 11th November, 2025

• National Unity Platform (NUP) presidential candidate Robert Kyagulanyi has pledged to unite Ugandans if elected, even as his campaign faced disruptions in Kiruhura and Kazo districts.

• Forum for Democratic Change (FDC) presidential candidate Nandala Mafabi has warned National Unity Platform (NUP) supporters against further confrontations, following clashes between the two groups in Budaka District

• Kampala Traders whose businesses were destroyed by last week’s floods in downtown Kampala have rejected Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja’s proposed condolences, insisting that the government must instead compensate them for their losses.

• Residents of Kabale Ward in Kitagwenda Town Council are breathing a sigh of relief after district authorities launched rehabilitation works on the 12-kilometer Katoma–Kyotamushana road, which has gone over 15 years without an upgrade.

• The Mpondwe Cross Border Traders Cooperative Society has demanded Shs317 million refund and Shs1 billion in compensation from Kasese District Local Government, citing a breach of contract over the management of Mpondwe-Lhubiri-ha Town Council Cattle Market at the Uganda-DR Congo border.

• Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr has declared a state of calamity after Typhoon Kalmaegi, one of the strongest typhoons this year, caused severe flooding in central Philippines, leaving at least 114 dead.

📸Courtsey

#CroozeFMNewsWrapUP
